newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana senator-elect to be sworn in.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana senator-elect to be sworn in.

text.p: Democrat Mary Landrieu of Louisiana will be sworn in as a senator next month while fraud charges in her election are being investigated, Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott said Tuesday.

Landrieu defeated Republican Woody Jenkins by less than 6,000 votes Nov. 5, but Jenkins claims at least 10,000 votes were fraudulently cast. They were running to replace retiring Democrat J. Bennett Johnston.
"We have received a request to look into this matter from Mr. Jenkins," Lott told reporters after he was re-elected without opposition as leader by fellow Republicans.

"We don't know exactly what the allegations are, what the evidence is. But we're in the process now of proceeding in a bipartisan way to make sure we look at it very carefully," the Mississippi Republican said.

"And the plan, at this time, would be then to swear Mary Landrieu in without prejudice. And that means not without prejudice just to her, but without prejudice to either person until the matter can be fully investigated," he added.
Swearing in Landrieu without prejudice would leave open the possibility that she could be removed if the Senate determines there was fraud in her election.
Democratic Leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota said he was confident Landrieu's victory would be upheld. "There is no validity whatsoever to the challenge," he said.
Senators elected on Nov. 5 are to be sworn in Jan. 7 when the next session of Congress begins. Republicans will have a 55-45 majority next year.
In January 1995, Democrat Dianne Feinstein of California was sworn in despite a challenge from her Republican opponent Michael Huffington. He conceded a month later.

The Senate ordered a new election in New Hampshire in 1975 when it could not determine who had won. The last senator removed from office because of a tainted election was Republican William Lorimer of Illinois in 1912.
